samples.summary: The new `currentViewMode !== 'edit'` guard on the theme repaint is bypassed by two other `renderPreview()` call sites, so the preview (and the mermaid engine) is rendered in `edit` mode anyway
samples.evidence: `setTheme` added `if (currentViewMode !== 'edit') renderPreview();` (editor.ts:443) and the new test asserts this avoids "download[ing] the mermaid engine for a pane nobody is looking at". But `renderPreview()` is called unconditionally from the update listener on every keystroke (`EditorView.updateListener.of((u) => { if (u.docChanged) renderPreview(); })`, editor.ts:326) and from the initial mount (editor.ts:343), neither of which checks `currentViewMode`. So in `edit` mode the very first keystroke — or even mounting a note that already contains a ```mermaid fence — calls `preview.render()`, which calls `renderMermaidBlocks` and dynamically imports mermaid + dompurify for a hidden pane. The guard therefore does not achieve what its comment and test claim; it only skips one of three paths.

samples.summary: `RENDER_CACHE_LIMIT = 40` is a global cap shared by all diagrams; a note with more than 40 mermaid fences self-evicts within a single pass and re-lays-out every diagram on every keystroke
samples.evidence: `remember()` evicts the LRU entry whenever `renderCache.size > 40`. In a note with N > 40 diagrams, a single `renderPass` inserts N entries, evicting entries it created earlier in that same pass. On the next `render()` (one per keystroke in split mode) `collectPending` therefore misses for the earlier diagrams, they flash back to their `<pre>` source, and the mermaid layout engine re-runs for all of them — the exact churn the cache exists to prevent. The limit is not per-preview or per-document, so it is also shared with any other cached sources.

samples.summary: A single transient failure of the `import('mermaid')` / `import('dompurify')` chunk fetch is memoized forever, permanently disabling diagrams for the rest of the session with no retry
samples.evidence: `loaded ??= import('mermaid')...catch(() => null)` (mermaid.ts:141-144) and `purifier ??= import('dompurify')...catch(() => null)` (mermaid.ts:158) store the *resolved-null* promise. Because `??=` only assigns when the variable is nullish and it is never reset outside `resetMermaidStateForTests()`, a one-off network blip during chunk download means `renderPass` bails at `if (!mermaid || !purify ...) return;` (mermaid.ts:431) for every subsequent pass — every diagram in every note stays a `<pre>` fallback until a full page reload, even after connectivity returns.

samples.summary: Failed renders are cached permanently per (theme, source), so a diagram that failed for a non-deterministic reason can never recover without a reload
samples.evidence: `remember(key, result)` (mermaid.ts:486) stores error outcomes in the same cache as successes, and nothing ever invalidates an error entry. The comment argues a failure is "a deterministic property of the source" because passes are serialized, but mermaid keeps process-global state (config from `initialize`, `maxTextSize`, internal id/error state), and the engine's own internal errors (e.g. a layout failure after a config change or a `maxEdges` trip) are not source-deterministic. Once cached, the identical source will show the stale `Diagram error:` label on every later render even if it would now succeed — including after a theme switch back to the theme it failed under.

samples.summary: `passChain` is a module-global, never-reset promise chain shared by every preview instance; a `mermaid.render()` that never settles stalls all future diagram rendering process-wide
samples.evidence: `let passChain: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();` (mermaid.ts:359) and `passChain = run` (mermaid.ts:414) serialize *all* passes, for all roots, through one chain. `renderPass` awaits `mermaid.render(...)` with no timeout (mermaid.ts:468). If that promise never settles (mermaid has known hangs on pathological/very large inputs) every subsequent `renderMermaidBlocks` call — including from a different note opened later in the same session — is queued behind it forever, and its blocks stay pending with no error label, since the `.catch` at mermaid.ts:410 only fires on rejection. There is also no reset when a preview is disposed.

samples.summary: Front matter is stripped unconditionally, so mermaid's documented `title:` / `displayMode:` front matter silently stops working for every diagram
samples.evidence: `stripConfigDirectives()` does `source.replace(FRONTMATTER_RE, '')` regardless of content (mermaid.ts:227). Any note using the standard `---\ntitle: My chart\n---` header — valid, widely documented mermaid — loses its title with no feedback. The JSDoc acknowledges the cost, but nothing surfaces it to the note author (no error label, no note in the design doc's user-facing behavior), so it will read as a rendering bug.

finding.summary: Narrowed ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP strips almost every SVG geometry/presentation attribute, so real diagrams render empty
finding.evidence: `ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP: /^(?:#|https?:\/\/|mailto:)/i` in PURIFY_CONFIG. DOMPurify's `_isValidAttribute` applies `IS_ALLOWED_URI` to the value of EVERY allowed attribute that is not in `DEFAULT_URI_SAFE_ATTRIBUTES` (`alt,class,for,id,label,name,pattern,placeholder,role,summary,title,value,style,xmlns`) and not `data-*`/`aria-*`; if the value matches neither the URI regexp nor the `data:`/ALLOW_UNKNOWN_PROTOCOLS fallbacks, the branch `else if (value) return false` drops the attribute. That is precisely why DOMPurify's DEFAULT regexp contains the permissive `[^a-z]|[a-z+.\-]+(?:[^a-z+.\-:]|$)` alternatives — to let non-URI values through. Replacing it with `^(?:#|https?://|mailto:)` therefore removes `d="M0,0 L4,2"`, `transform="translate(8,8)"`, `viewBox="0 0 100 100"`, `width/height/x/y`, `stroke-width="2"`, `fill="none"`, `text-anchor`, `points`, `marker-end="url(#id)"` (value starts with `u`, not `#`) etc. from mermaid's output, leaving a structurally-present but unrenderable SVG. No test catches this: every attribute in the fixtures at packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:357-386 is either `data-*` (`data-text`) or URI-safe (`id`, `class`, `style`, `href="#section"`), and real mermaid cannot run under jsdom, so the suite is green while the shipped feature paints blank diagrams.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise is factually wrong about the code. The only ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP in the repo is mermaid.ts:264-265: /^(?:(?:https?|mailto):|[^a-z]|[a-z+.\-]+(?:[^a-z+.\-:]|$))/i — DOMPurify's default with only the scheme list narrowed. Both permissive trailing alternatives the reviewer claims were removed ([^a-z] and [a-z+.\-]+(?:[^a-z+.\-:]|$)) are present, so d/transform/viewBox/width/height/fill="none"/stroke-width/text-anchor/marker-end="url(#arrow)" all match and are preserved; the in-code comment at mermaid.ts:256-263 documents exactly this reasoning. The claimed pattern /^(?:#|https?:\/\/|mailto:)/i appears nowhere (grep across repo returns only mermaid.ts:264, a doc line, and a test comment). The secondary claim of no test coverage is also false: preview.test.ts:497-532 is a dedicated test asserting survival of precisely that attribute set.
